cells.tense: Present tense — here, with the pen.
cells.verb: letting fall what has already stopped holding
cells.place: in the direction you have chosen
cells.ask: Offer to keep one small practice lit — a few quiet minutes of the thing you're refining, kept because it steadies you rather than because it proves anything. Practice flows without force, and the solitude of it connects rather than isolates.
cells.core: You're not pushing anything over. You're noticing what was already hollow and letting it go, and the letting-go is clean because you're not doing it to prove a point — you've simply stopped keeping weight on a beam that cracked and never carried. The direction you chose survives because it was never resting on the false thing. What you keep, you keep because it holds.
cells.sheetLine: The things that fall are the ones that needed to. You're choosing what stays.

cells.tense: Future tense — bracing at a future that can't be written in.
cells.place: in the direction you're trying to force into shape
cells.ask: Offer one thing you're probably going to need to your people first — not as a manifesto, but as something you'd want passed to you if it came from them. Living transmission of meaning moves through you and adapts; it doesn't demand the room agree before it's spoken. What comes back when this balances is a clearing that surprises you by how quiet it is.
cells.core: You can feel that something's false and you want it gone now — so you're breaking it early, before the truth that would break it has actually arrived. Every structure starts looking like a structure to tear down, and nothing gets to stand long enough to serve you. The chaos feels like freedom but it's just the next thing not standing. Some of what you're demolishing would have held.
cells.sheetLine: You're pulling things down before the real thing gets a chance to bring them down for you.

cells.tense: Past tense — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: holding up what has already stopped holding
cells.place: in the direction you're propping up rather than steering
cells.ask: Offer to put one small structure back under the thing you're actually doing now — a time, a place, a shape that makes it navigable. Authority doesn't mean control; it means things in your presence make sense. What comes back when this balances is a direction that carries you without your arms tired from propping it.
cells.core: You keep your hands under a beam that's already down. The plan, the version of the direction, the reason you gave for it — none of it is bearing weight anymore, and you're holding the shape because letting it fall would mean the decision is over. Nothing is holding it up but you. The choosing stopped; the bracing didn't.
cells.sheetLine: You're still holding up something that already came down.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: being the one who clears the false thing
cells.place: in the direction you're already choosing
cells.ask: Offer to notice one piece of the direction that was set by your own wanting and not by the situation — name it to yourself as yours. Movement from feeling is already how you're going; the ask is to let the wanting be visible in it. What comes back when this balances is a clearing you recognize as your own doing in the moment you're doing it.
cells.core: You're already choosing — you've been choosing this whole stretch — and you describe it as the situation sorting itself out. Some part of you has been letting go of what wasn't working, in small ways, all along. But the story you're telling has the pen in someone else's hand. The clearing is happening. The claim on it isn't.
cells.sheetLine: You're already choosing this. You just haven't said so.

flags.detail: "a while ago" — a cell knows no one's past
